dossier.public_summary: The fast 1.41-day dip is locked to the star's 1.4-day spin and shows out-of-eclipse brightness swings as big as the dip itself, plus a very high Gaia RUWE. That pattern points to a stellar eclipsing binary or active binary on the target star, not a 2.46 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: RUWE far above 1.4 indicates the Gaia astrometric solution is not a single star, supporting the binary/phase-curve interpretation over a quiet planet host.
Out-of-eclipse variation at the transit period is as large as the 2300 ppm dip itself with very high chi2, as expected for a synchronised stellar binary/ellipsoidal signal, not a planet.

The 1.41 d dip period is essentially the measured 1.40 d rotation/spot period, and the star shows 1-2% spot modulation, so the signal repeats at a multiple of the stellar variability with a non-transit shape.
Duration is 1.6x the central-duration expectation for a 0.4708 Rsun M dwarf with a negative density log ratio, long for a planet on target and consistent with a diluted or eccentric eclipsing binary.
On-target localization rules out the inspected neighbours as the source, so the large phase curve and RUWE must be intrinsic to the target, not a blended neighbour.
